original_test_intent: Visually verify the E1S indicator under the PSB topology for owner-defined green and amber solid/blink states.
original_method: A qualified on-site operator identifies the exact PSB-connected E1S LED, establishes only approved system and I/O states, captures timestamped color/cadence evidence, and leaves BMC-undefined or undefined amber states for owner disposition.
manual_activity: An on-site operator uses an owner-approved PSB/E1S state matrix, records direct LED color/cadence and physical context, and reports both unresolved amber states without inventing stimuli.
required_inputs: Exact PSB identity, E1S slot/drive/FRU and physical LED location
Owner correction for Green Solid being both on and off when system on
Precise system/drive/link states for green solid and off
Safe I/O stimulus and measurable green blink cadence/observation duration
BMC ownership and approved stimulus for Amber Solid or explicit not-applicable disposition
Definition/stimulus for Amber Blink or approved not-applicable disposition
LED legend, camera/viewing/color-reference requirements and PASS/FAIL matrix
Independent PSB/storage/BMC recovery and passive pre/post health checks
safety_requirements: Do not infer which green system-on statement is correct
Do not invent a BMC or CPLD stimulus for either amber state
Use only approved system/I/O states and keep hands clear of energized hardware
Do not reseat E1S, disconnect PSB paths, reset management controllers or alter link/power state unless separately authorized
Stop on storage/link error, unexpected LED, power/thermal/BMC anomaly or unsafe access
Do not accept remote telemetry as visual color/cadence proof
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact row and isolate both later I3C CPU1 duplicates
Organize PSB/E1S topology, corrected state matrix and evidence checklist
Collect passive storage/link/BMC health context around operator observation
Preserve timestamped photos/video and unresolved amber dispositions
Perform no direct visual verdict, BMC/CPLD stimulus, I/O generation, hardware action, retry or PASS/FAIL decision
engineer_actions: Correct the green solid/off conflict and define PSB/E1S state semantics
Approve safe I/O stimulus and measurable blink cadence
Define or explicitly exclude BMC Amber Solid and Amber Blink
Review evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Photograph the labeled PSB path and target E1S LED, record each approved state with timing and color references, and correlate passive storage/link health before restoration.

project_override_considerations: Hardware or BMC revisions that do not implement amber states require explicit revision-scoped N/A approval; absence is not an automatic PASS.

Approved PSB-to-E1S slot/device/LED topology and corrected green-state matrix
Safe I/O/cadence definition plus amber-solid and amber-blink dispositions
Timestamped contextual and close photo/video with color/timing reference
Passive pre/post drive, link, PSB and BMC/event health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1905 assigns both Green Solid On and Off to system on, while Amber Solid is BMC not defined and Amber Blink not defined. The two later same-code I3C/CPU1 variants are distinct and quarantined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The PSB-attached E1S visual purpose remains identifiable and manually executable once the owner corrects the state matrix and dispositions amber coverage.

review_improvement: Separates three same-code identities, records the green contradiction and makes PSB path/slot identity and both amber dispositions auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: On a PSB-attached storage path, an LED may reflect drive activity, slot power or enclosure management rather than the host-visible I/O state alone. The observation must therefore bind the exact drive, slot and PSB path and be correlated with passive link/storage health; otherwise a blink from background traffic can be misread as the intended stimulus response.
